body:
Seen in run 0442c97d6b8bf128 on task:be36c1d67353660d (steps 76–77). `*** Add: extract::rust::tests::an_inline_test_carries_a_crate_root_module`, written with `::` instead of `.` before the name, quietly created a new module `extract::rust::tests::an_inline_test_…` with the test function inside it. The worker only saw unrelated "cannot find `ready` / `Scratch` / `CARGO`" errors and had to work out what had happened.

- When an `*** Add:` header would create a new module whose only item has the same name as that module, refuse before type-checking and suggest `*** Add: <parent module>.<name>` (here `extract::rust::tests.an_inline_test_carries_a_crate_root_module`).
- Adding a real new module (a different name, or several items) is unchanged.

Check: a unit test where `*** Add: m::f` with a body of just `fn f() {}` is refused with the dotted suggestion, and `*** Add: m::helpers` with `fn f() {}` still creates the module.
title: submit: refuse Add that wraps an item in its own module
